business_summary: Xylem Inc. (NYSE: XYL) is a global water-technology company spun off from ITT Corporation in 2011, supplying pumps, treatment, metering, analytics and digital infrastructure for utility, industrial and commercial water and wastewater systems; it roughly doubled in scale after absorbing Evoqua Water Technologies in 2023. It sits on the data-center-moratoria chain's water-permitting-and-hydrology link (position 5, HIGH-criticality bottleneck): the chain names Xylem on retail stock lists built specifically around AI data-center water-permitting and hydrology constraints, the 'second permit nobody used to model' that the chain's own bottleneck note says now sits on the critical path beside the interconnection queue. SEC companyfacts gives revenue, operating income, cash flow, debt and a full quality block (Piotroski, Beneish, Altman, reverse DCF) current through FY2025 and the 2026-06-30 balance-sheet instant, with zero NULL canonical fields, the cleanest data coverage of the three names profiled this batch.

exposure_summary.narrative: Xylem has 1 placement on data-center-moratoria (water-permitting-and-hydrology, CROWDED, HIGH bottleneck criticality, not money-corner). The mapped role rests on a retail stock-screener article naming Xylem among water-infrastructure plays for AI data centers; no primary Xylem filing or investor material was fetched this run to size the data-center share of its roughly $9 billion of revenue, most of which still serves municipal, industrial and commercial water customers unrelated to data centers. The chain's own map_limitation records that water scarcity is designed away at the drawing board by closed-loop and direct-to-chip cooling, so the addressable opportunity is itself contested.

Measures how much of the expectation reading is a horizon convention rather than a statement about price, and inherits the same assumed discount rate and terminal growth.

crowdedness_caveats: The water-permitting-and-hydrology link carries a crowdedness score of 62 and verdict CROWDED: the chain's own heat rationale says the crowding is on the names, not on the mechanism, with AI water-scarcity stock lists ranking names by hedge fund ownership. Xylem sits at only the 9.8th percentile of its own three-year price range as of 2026-08-28, against a five-name median of 63.9 (PNR 0.9, XYL 9.8, AWK 63.9, ECL 95.6, WTS 96.2), the widest dispersion the heat map records on this chain.

The chain's own map_limitation states that closed-loop and direct-to-chip cooling designs substitute the water constraint away at the drawing board, and that the whole national data-center water draw is under 1 percent of US water consumption (ITIF), so the scarcity this link prices is local and political rather than physical and universal.

No pcs (positioning/crowdedness) block exists locally for data/market/XYL.json to corroborate the read at the issuer level; the crowdedness signal above is the chain link's own heat score, not issuer-level positioning data.
